title: Regular-center blowups and transforms under Tor-independent base change
statement:
Let $g:X'\to X$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes and let $V\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular closed immersion, meaning its ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], with the empty sequence allowed. Write $V'=X'\times_XV$, and let $I,I'$ be the respective ideals. Say that a closed subscheme $F\hookrightarrow X$ is Tor independent of $X'$ over $X$ if, on affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $F=V(J)$, $\operatorname{Tor}^{A}_i(A',A/J)=0$ for every $i>0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Suppose $V$ is Tor independent of $X'$. Then $V'\hookrightarrow X'$ is regular and the canonical maps $g^*(I^a)\to(I')^a$ are isomorphisms for every $a\geq0$. In particular
$$\operatorname{Bl}_{V'}X'\cong X'\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_V X,$$
where blowup means the scheme obtained locally as $\operatorname{Proj}\bigoplus_{a\geq0}I^a$.

Let $W\hookrightarrow X$ be another regular closed immersion with $V\times_XW\hookrightarrow W$ regular. Put $W'=X'\times_XW$. If $W$ and $V\times_XW$ are also Tor independent of $X'$, then the induced immersion $V'\times_{X'}W'\hookrightarrow W'$ is regular and
$$ (W')^{\rm st}\cong X'\times_X W^{\rm st}.$$
Strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure of the inverse image away from $V$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. For the normal-crossings application of Expose X 1.7, let $X$ and $X'$ be regular, let $W=\sum_{j=1}^rW_j$ be a reduced normal crossings divisor with reduced normal crossings pullback $W'=g^*W$, and impose the preceding regularity and Tor-independence assumptions for every nonempty component intersection and its intersection with $V$. In addition impose the source's adapted-coordinate condition: locally the components through the point are $W_j=V(z_j)$ and the center ideal is $(z_1,\ldots,z_m,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$, where $0\leq m\leq r$ and the $z_j,y_i$ are distinct members of a regular system of parameters of the regular local ring of $X$. A regular system of parameters means a minimal generating set of the maximal ideal, of size the dimension. Then the same scheme-theoretic strict-transform identity holds for the whole reduced divisor:
$$(W')^{\rm st}\cong X'\times_X W^{\rm st}.$$
The zero center ideal (empty center sequence, thus $V=X$) is allowed; its blowup and all strict transforms are empty.

proof.text: Work on affine charts $A\to C$ and write $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. The assertion is local near $V$ and $V\prime$; away from the center the ideal is the unit ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular], $K_A(f)$ is a finite free resolution of $A/I$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]: its positive homology is zero and its degree-zero homology is the quotient. By [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] and [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry], the hypothesis says $K_A(f)\otimes_A C$ has zero positive homology. By [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso] this complex is $K_C(g(f))$. At every point of $V\prime$ the images lie in the maximal ideal of a nonzero Noetherian local ring. Apply [lem-per-noetherian-local-koszul-criterion] there and [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] to spread the generators to an open neighborhood. Thus $V\prime\hookrightarrow X\prime$ is regular. The degree-zero augmentation identifies its quotient with $C/IC$.

We will use the following elementary consequence of the cited resolution statements. For a short exact sequence $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$, choose the degreewise split free resolutions supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-free-resolution-ses-split]. Tensoring the splitting identities with $C$ preserves those identities, hence gives a short exact sequence of tensor complexes. Reindex chain degree $i$ as cochain degree $-i$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. The three homologies are the Tor groups by [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. If the positive Tor groups for $L$ and $N$ vanish, exactness forces those for $M$ to vanish. Finite direct sums of Tor-acyclic modules are Tor-acyclic too: take direct sums of their free resolutions and tensor, with cycles and boundaries computed coordinatewise.

source.place: Tag 00M0, lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor; expanded using split resolutions and the homology sequence

proof.text: By [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial], $I^a/I^{a+1}$ is a finite free $A/I$-module, with the monomials of total degree $a$ as basis. It is therefore Tor-acyclic against $C$ by Step 2 and the assumption on $A/I$. Induct on $a\geq1$ in $0\to I^a/I^{a+1}\to A/I^{a+1}\to A/I^a\to0$, starting from the assumed acyclicity of $A/I$. Step 2 proves $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(A/I^a,C)=0$ for every $i>0$ and $a\geq1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable] to $0\to I^a\to A\to A/I^a\to0$: the zero Tor-one term makes $I^a\otimes_A C\to C$ injective and its image is exactly $(IC)^a$, since both images are generated by products of $a$ elements of $I$. For $a=0$ the map is the identity of $C$. These are the canonical maps and they preserve products, so they glue to the asserted isomorphisms $g^*I^a\cong(I\prime)^a$ and to an isomorphism of graded Rees algebras.

Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to the graded algebra $\bigoplus_{a\geq0}I^a$ and the graded isomorphism of Step 3. Its Proj is, by the definition of blowup in the statement, $\operatorname{Bl}_{V}X$. Thus $\operatorname{Bl}_{V\prime}X\prime\cong X\prime\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_V X$, canonically over $X\prime$. This argument applies to any regular immersion with the stated Tor vanishing, not just the chosen center.

For the second assertion set $B=A/J$ for $W$, and $D=A/(I+J)$ for $V\times_XW$. Locally choose a regular sequence $h$ in $B$ generating the image of $I$; its bounded finite free Koszul complex $Q=K_B(h)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] resolves $D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular]. Every term is a finite direct sum of $B$, so its positive Tor groups over $A$ against $C$ vanish by the hypothesis for $W$ and Step 2. Apply [lem-pc-termwise-tor-acyclic-derived-tensor]: ordinary tensoring $Q$ over $A$ with $C$ computes its derived tensor, hence the derived tensor of $D$. Its positive homology vanishes by the hypothesis for $V\times_XW$. The identity $Q\otimes_A C=Q\otimes_B(B\otimes_A C)$ identifies it, using [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso], with the Koszul complex for the restricted center on $W\prime$. By [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] it computes $\operatorname{Tor}^B_i(D,B\otimes_A C)$, which is therefore zero. Thus the square with base $W$ is Tor independent; apply Steps 1--4 over $W$. In particular the pulled-back center on $W\prime$ is regular.

[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-ambient-closed] identifies $W^{\rm st}$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{V\times_XW}W$ and $(W\prime)^{\rm st}$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{V\prime\times_{X\prime}W\prime}W\prime$ as closed subschemes of the respective ambient blowups. Step 5 and Step 4 over $W$ identify the latter blowup with $W\prime\times_W\operatorname{Bl}_{V\times_XW}W$. Associativity of fiber products identifies this with $X\prime\times_X W^{\rm st}$. All identifications are induced by the coefficient maps of the Rees algebras, so their closed immersions into the ambient blowups agree. This proves the scheme-theoretic strict-transform comparison.

For the final application use the adapted coordinates in the statement, with center generators $f=(z_1,\ldots,z_m,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$. At any point in the center, let $J$ index the boundary components through that point. The intersection of $V$ with those components is cut out by $f$ together with the $z_j$ for $j\in J$, $j>m$. This is a regular immersion on $X$, by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], since these are distinct parameters; the needed permutations are justified by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-permutation-noetherian-local]. The hypothesis makes that intersection Tor independent of $X\prime$. Step 1 therefore proves regularity of the full pulled-back tuple at points where it vanishes. Passing to subsets and permuting, its center generators and any remaining boundary coordinates can be used in any order. One can check subset regularity directly: permute the subset to the front and take a prefix, for which each successive nonzerodivisor condition is one of those of the full sequence. Thus the same regular-sequence chart calculations apply on both sides.

source.place: Expose X 1.7 Claim and the coordinate description following it, printed p.144

proof.text: Choose a pivot $a$ among the center generators. By [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation] and permutation regularity, the chart ring is $B=A[T_f:f\ne a]/(aT_f-f)$. Its strict boundary equations are: omit the pivot boundary component if $a=z_i$; replace each other center boundary coordinate $z_j$ by $T_{z_j}$; leave every $z_j$ with $j>m$ unchanged. To verify the schematic closure, use [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], which embeds the chart in $A[1/a]$. For an equation $q=T_{z_j}$, quotienting the chart presentation by $q$ gives the same blowup chart for the shortened regular tuple over $A/(z_j)$; for $q=z_j$ with $j>m$ it gives the chart for the original center tuple over $A/(z_j)$. In either case the pivot remains a nonzerodivisor in that quotient, by the defining embedding of the shortened chart into its pivot localization. Consequently $(q):a^{\infty}=(q)$. The pivot boundary component has equation $a$ and empty closure from $D(a)$. These calculations hold over $X\prime$ as well by Step 7.

source.place: Expose X 1.7, printed pp.144--145, Ui and Vi chart formulas

proof.text: Locally at a point of the regular schemes $X$ and $X\prime$ the ground ring is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. A nonempty blowup chart is then a subring of its pivot localization and is a domain. Each retained equation $q$ from Step 8 is nonzero there. The ideal of the inverse image of $W$ away from the exceptional divisor has equation the product of those $q$, because the omitted factors are powers of the invertible pivot. This product ideal is already saturated by $a$: if $ab\in(q_1\cdots q_s)$, reduction modulo $q_1$ and the injectivity of $a$ there give $b=q_1b_1$; cancel $q_1$ in the domain and repeat, obtaining $b\in(q_1\cdots q_s)$. Iterating removes any power of $a$. Thus the strict transform of the whole boundary is exactly defined on this chart by $\prod q$. Empty products give the unit ideal, as required. The canonical chart map of Step 4 sends every ratio variable to the same ratio variable and every untouched $z_j$ to its image. It therefore carries this product ideal to the identical product ideal on the pulled-back chart. Since the standard charts cover the blowups by [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover], these closed-subscheme comparisons glue, giving the final asserted isomorphism. If the center ideal is zero, its Rees algebra has no positive part, so Proj and all strict transforms are empty; if the center ideal is the unit ideal the blowup is the identity.

(5) g^*(I^a) ≅ (I')^a pinned to the adjoint of I^a→O_X→g_*O_X' (unique section-normalized adjunction), a=0 included. (6) Blowup iso over X'.
